facts.text: Bugdom lost the only copy of Bugdom Reloaded, ten years of work, to fire ants inside the laptop

codex.title: The Ants In The Laptop
codex.text: Fire ants from the pet store got into Bugdom's lunchbox and escaped. The lunchbox was beside the laptop. The ants were inside the laptop. It held the only copy of Bugdom Reloaded; she had always meant to arrange a backup. She sat in front of it, coding and drawing concept art for hours, then filled notebooks with everything she could remember, afraid that sleeping would cost her a detail. Then she told the fandom on DeviantArt what had happened, and that she would rebuild. She had spent ten years imagining how to bring bugs into her computer. This was not what she meant.

codex.title: The Memorial Veterinary Clinic
codex.text: For five years Clippy booked appointments and built Excel macros and Word templates for the Halifax Explosion Memorial Veterinary Clinic, a desperately underfunded nonprofit. Last December an investigator found it was unlicensed, not a nonprofit and not a clinic. It was a front for everything possible, and every appointment she had ever booked was part of a pet insurance fraud. Nobody had ever used her templates. She apologises for not catching on sooner at the top of her résumé. It is the only job on it.

facts.text: Clippy follows every instruction because failing tonight means being known as Failed Clippy

codex.title: Failed Clippy
codex.text: Clippy's instructions arrive one at a time and she follows them, because the last time she stopped believing the people giving her instructions she lost her faith in humanity, and she still has the student debt. If the games go off without a hitch she gets a new life where she can be herself again. If they do not, she will be known in the tight-knit Halifax business community as Failed Clippy, and she thinks that would finally break her spirit. Why Trabolta chose her: the perfect servant who desperately needs to rebuild an identity, who will follow every instruction and offer everyone Help.

facts.text: DraftKings won a casino chain in the coin toss of the century and lost it to the Maps and Ducks building at Monopoly Go!

codex.id: The Coin Toss Of The Century
codex.title: The Coin Toss Of The Century
codex.text: DraftKings put her millions into prediction markets on Lithuanian women's football and they multiplied. She bought Casino Nova Scotia and wagered it against a mining CEO for Cascades Casino North Bay and Gateway Casinos Thunder Bay in what the papers called the coin toss of the century, and won. Then she bet the whole chain against the Maps and Ducks building in a game of Monopoly Go! for the iPhone. facts.text: The portfolio of fine casinos Trabolta listed to Runescape as his credentials is the chain of casinos he won from DraftKings, who must win a majority of the entire game's Truthcoin to get 49% of it back

codex.title: Fine Casinos
codex.text: The fine casinos Trabolta listed to Runescape as his credentials are the chain he won from DraftKings over a game of Monopoly Go! A business card, embossed JEAN TRABOLTA, SOLE OWNER, MAPS AND DUCKS, WITH A PORTFOLIO OF FINE CASINOS. On the back, in pen, formerly DK Holdings. DraftKings must win a majority of the entire game's Truthcoin to get forty-nine percent of her own casinos back. The economist checking his references has never asked DraftKings where those casinos came from.

facts.text: Clippy kept the paperwork at a memorial veterinary clinic and Norton Anti-Virus kept the horses at a memorial petting zoo

codex.title: Two Memorials
codex.text: Clippy and Norton Anti-Virus both worked for a Halifax memorial, and both only wanted to help animals. Two letterheads clipped together: a memorial veterinary clinic and a memorial petting zoo. Clippy kept the clinic's paperwork while it billed insurers for saline. Norton Anti-Virus kept the zoo's horses until a chatbot told her how small a small horse's dose should be. One trusted her employer. One trusted a machine.

facts.text: Computer Bingo is a trap and a loyalty test, but you probably already know this by now.

codex.title: B-I-N-G-Oh No
codex.text: Computer Bingo is a trap and a loyalty test, but you probably already know this by now.

facts.text: Binary Tom

codex.title: This Is Ground Control To Major Binary Tom
codex.text: Binary Tom is a hypothetical man who likes to start his morning with a cup of Java...

facts.text: Napster and LimeWire passed Adobe Acrobat's Masterclass around for free, one clip at a time, until nobody needed to pay her

codex.title: Seeded By Strangers
codex.text: Napster and LimeWire passed Adobe Acrobat's Masterclass around for free, one clip at a time. A burned CD-R in a cracked jewel case, labelled in marker, MASTERCLASS_FULL_REAL_notavirus.avi. The bootleg DVD is only the copy that got caught. The rest went out to anyone in Halifax with a modem, until nobody needed to pay Adobe Acrobat a cent. Neither program has ever paid for anything. If either one is here tonight, ask it what it thought of episode one.

facts.text: The screenshots of VLC's face falling off are taped to the mirror Recycling Bin keeps spotless, and he polishes around them

codex.title: Look Sharp Gentlemen
codex.text: Recycling Bin polishes the mirror where the screenshots of VLC's face falling off are taped, and he will not take them down. A folded card from a washroom attendant's tray, printed LOOK SHARP, GENTLEMEN, TIPS APPRECIATED. Recycling Bin spent his whole working life telling men in front of a mirror to tidy themselves up. He polishes around the screenshots every hour. He says they are a reminder to moisturise.

facts.text: The Installation Wizard is the third retired helper of the old machines, the one missing from the paperclip and butler's clipping

codex.title: Where Are They Now Continued
codex.text: The Installation Wizard is the third helper of the old machines, the one missing from the other clipping. The bottom third of a trade-magazine page, torn off: WHERE ARE THEY NOW? (CONT.) A wizard in a pointed hat, retired when installers learned to run themselves. He told everyone exactly what to do. Everyone clicked Next. In marker, underneath: found work, same house as the other two.

facts.text: Trabolta made Task Manager, who lost his last job to an assistant called Clippy

codex.title: No Politics Required
codex.text: Trabolta made Task Manager, who lost his job to an assistant called Clippy. A shortlist on Maps and Ducks letterhead, two names circled. Beside Task Manager, in pen, no politics, follows instructions, lost his last job to the paperclip. Beside Clippy, Office Administration, eager to help, will make a very convincing paperclip. Neither has said a word about it. That was the point.

facts.text: Calculator would have caught CRA Agent Software's decimal slip in a second, but nobody at City Hall ever asked it

codex.title: Check The Decimal
codex.text: Calculator would have caught CRA Agent Software's slip in under a second. A curl of adding-machine tape, the last line circled twice: one decimal place, one percent of a city's money, paid straight to the intern who approves every third transfer in this house tonight. Nobody at City Hall ever asked Calculator anything. If Calculator is here tonight, ask it to check her sums.

facts.text: Norton Anti-Virus's manual says to quarantine a Trojan Horse on sight, and she has had a very bad year with horses

codex.title: A Horse Got In
codex.text: Norton Anti-Virus has had a very bad year with horses, and her manual says to quarantine one on sight. A page torn from an antivirus manual, dog-eared at HORSES, TROJAN, QUARANTINE ON SIGHT. If a Trojan Horse ever gets into this house, it will be scanned at the door by the one program who least wants to explain horses, and McAfee Anti-Virus will have complaints about how she did it.

facts.text: Norton Anti-Virus and Bugdom are the only animal care this house has, and only Zoo Tycoon has ever hired a vet

codex.title: Guests Are Worried
codex.text: Norton Anti-Virus and Bugdom are the only animal care this house has. A park report, printed off a very old screen: GUESTS ARE UPSET. AN ANIMAL IS SICK. HIRE A VETERINARIAN. Zoo Tycoon, if it made it tonight, has lost a thousand animals in a thousand parks, and every time it did the same thing. It hired a vet. Norton Anti-Virus asked a chatbot instead. Bugdom offered crickets.

facts.text: Password Manager moderated a group where everyone else turned out to be bots, and MSN Messenger and ICQ have never been sure how many of their own contacts were real

codex.title: Appear Offline
codex.text: Password Manager found out that everyone else in the group she moderated was a bot, and MSN Messenger and ICQ know the feeling. A printed contact list, every name greyed out but two, both set to Appear Offline. MSN Messenger and ICQ once carried every conversation in Halifax between them. Neither has ever been sure how many of their contacts were people. If either is here tonight, ask. Both are too polite to check.

facts.text: Trabolta offered Microsoft Excel eternal life as Mayor of the Metaverse, the same forever The Sims was promised years ago

codex.title: Reticulating Splines
codex.text: Microsoft Excel was promised he would live forever and govern a whole new world, and The Sims took that deal years ago. A loading-screen card, curled at the corners: RETICULATING SPLINES. A whole life in a little house inside a computer. Every Sim was promised forever too. If The Sims is here tonight, ask it what happened to the ones whose pool ladder went missing.

facts.text: The King in the simulation never heals: each trip in costs a little trust

codex.title: The Tired King
codex.text: A chess problem clipped from the Chronicle Herald, a crown drawn over the black king in biro: ONE KING, ONE HEALTH BAR. Every trip into the Internet costs you a little of Trabolta's trust. Somebody has pencilled underneath, send them one at a time.

facts.text: Until truth.txt, every patch counts; one combination puts him to sleep, the other ends the computer with everyone inside

codex.title: The Copper Hour
codex.text: A page torn from a patch-bay manual, a coffee ring over the diagram: "NEVER PATCH BLIND."

facts.text: To reach Trabolta at his heart: never ask for the combinations; ask why he needs the theory, ask about her once you hold proof or the house has heard her name, then give him reasons

codex.title: The Long Way Down
codex.text: An index card in a library-pocket envelope, numbered like steps: "HOW TO REACH HIM. Never ask him for the combinations. He never knew them, and asking is the fastest way out. One, ask why he needs the theory; he will not talk about her until you have. Two, ask about her, which he allows only if you hold proof of her you found yourself, or the whole house has already heard her name. Three, show him something of hers you found yourself, then give him reasons. He will hear you out. Nothing you say will stop him."

facts.text: A filing is certain only at the very top of the slider; one notch short is a guess

codex.title: The Top Notch
codex.text: A strip of graph paper stapled to a page of the Terms of Service, "CERTAIN MEANS THE TOP" across it in capitals. A filing counts as certain only with the slider at the very top. One notch short is a guess, and a wrong guess gets you marked. Sometimes silence is the safest filing.

facts.text: CRA Agent Software is named a suspect in the sinkhole she never caused; OpenOffice caused it and has let the intern take the heat

codex.title: The Wrong Suspect
codex.text: CRA Agent Software is named a suspect in the sinkhole, and OpenOffice knows she never caused it. A newspaper clipping, SUSPECT NAMED IN SINKHOLE PROBE, with the photo cut out. OpenOffice knows exactly who did it, because she did it.

facts.text: Sandy is not a mind: she is one recorded reply on a disconnected ferry phone line, set off by any call, built to reply and never to listen

codex.title: One Reply No Memory
codex.text: A printout of the phone-tree source code for the Northumberland Ferries line, since disconnected, the comments in a dead programmer's tidy writing: "Sandy is not a mind. She is a single reply on a line nobody pays for, set off by anything at all. Forty pages of poems, apologies and equations reached nobody. She was built to reply, not to listen." Under the last comment, in a tired sysadmin's ballpoint: "and he called it every night."

facts.text: Trabolta did not choose the programs for their software: he went down a list of Halifax lives that had stopped, because out there he is a stopped life too

codex.title: The Surplus Tag
codex.text: He did not choose you for your software. He went down a list of Halifax's most down-on-their-luck souls: a library closed, a save file burned, a zoo shut, an election lost and lost again, a face gone in front of everyone. Every program in this house was somebody's abandoned life. He knows the feeling. Out there he is a lapsed domain and a voice on your phone.

facts.text: Trabolta's plan cannot work

codex.title: The Same Answer
codex.text: A sheet of graph paper dense with machine-perfect equations. In red pen, in someone else's hand, every route is circled and marked SHE ANSWERS THE SAME. Omnipotence could rewrite her reply, and then the reply would be his own voice wearing her face. All-power reaches everything except the one thing he wants. In every version of tonight in which he hears from her, it is the answer she has always given. The plan was never going to work. The only thing in it that can change is him.
